data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims the 'single best' cross-city modulator is city size because larger cities integrate a greater area of impervious surface. But the cross-city nocturnal UHI gap is an intensive temperature difference (city-center minus rural), not an extensive quantity that necessarily grows with area. If you compare two cities of different footprint but identical built density, vegetation cover, anthropogenic heat flux density, and aridity, the nocturnal UHI intensity (ΔT) can be the same. City size scales total stored heat, but ΔT is governed by per-area fluxes and radiative cooling efficiency, so city size is not the best single modulator.
